english.notes:
(i) 'Dangerously out of control' is defined in section 10(3) of the Dangerous Dogs Act 1991 as being when there are grounds for reasonable apprehension that it will injure any person, whether or not it does so. This definition is not exclusive and the courts will adopt a straight forward interpretation of the words used in section 3 and look for any evidence that a dog is dangerously out of control by the way it behaves and whether it is under the control of the owner or person in charge of the dog. This definition does not include dogs being used for lawful purposes by the police or a person in the service of the crown, therefore dogs being used lawfully by the police, prison service, military police, and customs and excise, are exempt.
(ii) As from 13th May 2014, it is no longer a requirement for the dog to be in a public place. The offence may be committed if the dog is dangerously out of control in 'any place'. For offences committed before this date, H5242 should be used.
(iii) In proceedings for this offence against an owner who was not in charge of the dog, it is a defence under section 3(2) to prove that the dog was, at the material time, in the charge of a person whom he reasonably believed to be fit and proper to be in charge of it.
(iv) Section 3(1B) provides a defence in 'householder cases' - i.e. the dog is in a dwelling and the person in relation to whom the dog is dangerously out of control is in, or is entering, the dwelling as a trespasser (or the defendant believed this to be the case).
(v) Under section 4(1) the court may make a destruction order and may disqualify the offender from keeping a dog.
(vi) For the aggravated version of this offence (where injury or death is caused to a person/assistance dog) see H11472, H11474 and H11475

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
